bib.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery

read.skipped: Appendix C idea lists and D.1-D.10 generated papers were skimmed (reviews, scores, headers) not read line by line; they are model-written papers.

question: Can frontier LLMs run the whole ML research loop (idea, code, experiments, paper, review) with no human in it, and at what cost and quality?
hypothesis: An end-to-end LLM pipeline with an automated reviewer can produce papers that reach conference-level scores at low cost.
contributions: First end-to-end framework for fully automated scientific discovery in ML (idea generation, experiment, visualisation, write-up).
An LLM-based reviewing process with near-human performance on ICLR 2022 OpenReview data.
Hundreds of medium-quality papers over a week; case study and aggregate results.
Discussion of limitations, ethics and outlook.

method.summary: Three phases driven by LLMs: idea generation with Semantic Scholar novelty filter, experiment iteration through the Aider coding assistant on a small code template, and LaTeX paper write-up; then a GPT-4o reviewer scores the paper. Run with Sonnet 3.5, GPT-4o, DeepSeek Coder and Llama-3.1 405b on three templates.
method.task: automated ML research (ideation, coding, experiments, writing, review)

datasets.name: ICLR 2022 OpenReview papers
datasets.preprocessing: text of PDF via PyMuPDF; accepted papers are camera-ready, rejected are original submissions

datasets.name: 2D diffusion template (tiny-diffusion)
datasets.size: four 2D distributions (shapes, two moons, dinosaur, etc.)

inference.samples: ~50 generated ideas per run per template per model plus 1-2 seed ideas; single run per cell; reviewer: 5 ensembled reviews
inference.prompting: chain-of-thought and self-reflection; Aider with SEARCH/REPLACE edits; per-section writing with 'How to ML Paper' tips; reviewer on NeurIPS guidelines with 1 few-shot example
inference.retrieval: Semantic Scholar API for novelty check (10 rounds) and citations (20 rounds), top 10 results per query with abstracts

other.hardware: 8x NVIDIA H100 node, ~12 hours per run of ~50 ideas

metrics.name: Reviewer: balanced accuracy, accuracy, F1, AUC, FPR, FNR
metrics.definition: Reviewer accept/reject vs ICLR 2022 decisions on 500 papers; mean and 95% bootstrap CI; thresholded variant @6 (@8 for Sonnet)

metrics.name: Automated review score of generated papers
metrics.definition: NeurIPS overall score 1-6 style from the GPT-4o reviewer; mean and max per run

metrics.name: Counts of novel ideas / experiments passed / completed papers
metrics.definition: Novelty is self-assessed by each model via Semantic Scholar

eval.protocol: No external human evaluation of generated papers; one run per model and template; reviewer thresholds chosen on the evaluation set; case study judged by the authors.

availability.data: ICLR 2022 OpenReview dump (Berto 2024); generated papers, run files and logs in the repo

prompts.text: You are an ambitious AI PhD student who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.

You are an AI researcher who is reviewing a paper that was submitted to a prestigious ML venue. Be critical and cautious in your decision. If a paper is bad or you are unsure, give it bad scores and reject it.

You are an Area Chair at a machine learning conference. You are in charge of meta-reviewing a paper that was reviewed by {reviewer_count} reviewers. Your job is to aggregate the reviews into a single meta-review in the same format. Be critical and cautious in your decision, find consensus, and respect the opinion of all the reviewers.

results.claim: A generated paper costs about $10-15, from run cost divided by generated papers (not accepted papers).
results.setup: Three small ML templates, four LLMs, ~50 ideas per run; denominator is completed papers; no human labour or template-building cost counted.
results.quote: When dividing the number of generated papers by the total cost, we end up at a cost of around $10-15 per paper.

results.claim: Abstract headline: each idea is developed into a full paper at under $15.
results.setup: Abstract; same denominator issue.
results.quote: at a meager cost of less than $15 per paper

results.claim: GPT-4o reviewer with 5 reflections, 5 ensembled reviews and 1-shot example reaches 70% accuracy on ICLR 2022 decisions, below humans' 73%.
results.setup: 500 ICLR 2022 papers from OpenReview, text parsed with PyMuPDF; uncalibrated GPT-4o (1-shot) row; human number from NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment.
results.quote: With GPT-4o, The AI Scientist’s reviewing procedure achieves 70% accuracy when

results.claim: Calibrated GPT-4o (1-shot) thresholded at score 6 has balanced accuracy 0.65 vs human 0.66.
results.setup: 500 ICLR 2022 papers; threshold 6 chosen on the same data (no held-out set reported); mean +/- 95% bootstrap CI.
results.note: Text prints '0.65% vs. 0.66%' (typo for fractions); abstract-level contribution list says '65% vs. 66%'.
results.table: Table 1, row GPT-4o (1-shot) @6, column Balanced Acc.: 0.65 ± 0.04; row Human (NeurIPS): 0.66

results.claim: Calibrated GPT-4o (1-shot) @6 reaches F1 0.57 vs human 0.49 and equal AUC 0.65.
results.setup: Same as above; Accuracy for this row is 0.66, so the 70% accuracy and F1 0.57 come from different settings.

limits: Authors concede: reviewer data (ICLR 2022) may be in pretraining data; accepted papers are camera-ready while rejected are original submissions.
No vision: cannot read plots; tables overflow, figures mis-referenced.
Aider fails to implement many ideas; ideas repeat across runs.
Few experiments per idea so results lack rigor; unfair parameter/FLOP comparisons give deceptive conclusions.
Hallucinated results and hardware; incorrect implementations hard to catch; minimal sandboxing.
Templates are tiny (2D diffusion, NanoGPT, grokking) and datasets externally constrained.
Cost excludes human work for templates and verification; no external peer review of generated papers; threshold choice not held out.
Novelty check is self-assessed by each model.
